b.x: This is a map of what science describes today. It is not a diagnosis and it does not replace a doctor. Imaging studies vary in size. They do not promise that one minute a day rebuilds gray matter. If the wish is to die, in Brazil dial 188. This page does not dial.

You do not see the whole world. You see what attention selected. The rest can be in front of the eye and not enter. That is inattentional blindness: the film inside occupies the channel and the gorilla walks by. Working memory holds little. What was not attended is barely recorded. That is why two people on the same sidewalk report two streets. It is not morality. It is a channel limit. The gray man does not try to see everything. He chooses what matters in the room: the exit, the hands, who changed course. The rest can wait.

The most useful map splits attention into three jobs. Alerting: the body gets ready. A brainstem nucleus that uses noradrenaline takes part. It is the tone of someone who can act, not panic. Orienting: pointing the focus at a place, a sound, a face. Parietal areas and the frontal eye field take part. Controlling: staying, inhibiting the impulse, switching when the focus was wrong. The prefrontal cortex and the anterior cingulate take part. The one-minute practice uses all three. The air settles an exaggerated alert. The foot is the target of orienting. The name thought is control calling the focus back when it escaped.

When the task ends, another network takes over. It rehearses the past, the future, and the self. It is useful for planning. It becomes a prison when it does not switch off: rumination, the old sentence, the repeated fear. Threat and novelty also seize the focus from below, before the decision. A tone of voice, a no, a compliment. The salience network marks that as urgent. The prefrontal arrives later. That is why the emotional trigger speaks first and the belief arrives half a second behind. Naming the feeling is not magic. It gives the prefrontal a job, and that job often lowers the volume of the alarm. It does not erase the memory. It opens the gap.

The brain changes with what repeats. That is plastic, not a promise of sainthood. Returning to the foot, many times, is repeating control winning over the seizure. Sleep firms what was trained. Without sleep, the prefrontal tires first and attention drops. That is why the practice does not compete with the night. Closing the eyes on the street switches off orienting to the room. The map asks the opposite: focus on the foot and the exit still visible. Neuroscience does not ask you to become a monk. It asks you to know which network is in command. If it is the film, return. If it is real danger, act. The stroke does not wait for the minute to end.
